topic: What one unit of alcohol actually looks like

scenes.line: Is one glass of wine one unit? Usually not.
scenes.visual: Flat poster wine glass on an apricot block with an ink chip '= 1 unit?'; a bold ink cross stamps over the chip
scenes.animation: Block wipes up from the bottom at start; glass drops in on 'glass'; chip pops on 'unit' (back.out); cross draws on 'not'

scenes.line: In the UK, one unit is 10 millilitres of pure alcohol.
scenes.visual: Big teal block with a huge serif '10 ml' and an ink chip 'NHS: 1 unit' plus a label 'of pure alcohol'
scenes.animation: Block scales up from 0.8 at start; chip pops on 'UK'; number slides up on '10'; label fades on 'pure'

scenes.line: That's a single 25 millilitre shot of spirits.
scenes.visual: Flat shot glass filled with apricot liquid beside a big serif '25 ml' and a teal chip '= 1 unit'
scenes.animation: Glass slides in from the left at start; liquid rises from 0 on 'single'; number pops on '25'; chip pops on 'shot'

scenes.line: A standard 175 millilitre glass of wine is just over 2 units.
scenes.visual: Flat wine glass on the left; on the right a column of two full unit tiles plus a thin sliver tile, and a big serif '2.1' with a chip '175 ml glass'
scenes.animation: Glass slides up at start; chip pops on '175'; unit tiles stack with 0.15 s stagger on 'just'; '2.1' pops on 'units'

scenes.line: A pint of strong lager is 3.
scenes.visual: Flat pint glass of lager with foam on an ink block; three apricot unit tiles stacked beside it with a huge serif '3'
scenes.animation: Block wipes in at start; pint rises on 'pint'; three tiles stack with 0.1 s stagger and the '3' pops on '3'

scenes.line: The NHS advises no more than 14 units a week,
scenes.visual: Teal block with an ink chip 'NHS' and a huge serif '14' with a label 'units a week, at most'
scenes.animation: Block scales up from 0.8 at start; chip pops on 'NHS'; '14' slides up on '14'; label fades on 'week'
scenes.onScreenText: NHS: no more than 14 a week

scenes.visual: A row of seven flat day tiles (M T W T F S S); three of them fill apricot with small unit marks, the rest stay paper
scenes.animation: Day tiles fade in with 0.05 s stagger at start; three tiles fill apricot one by one (stagger 0.15 s) on '3'

scenes.line: In the US, a standard drink is bigger: 14 grams of alcohol, compared with 8 grams in a UK unit.
scenes.visual: Two blocks side by side: a taller ink block 'US drink 14 g' and a shorter teal block 'UK unit 8 g', bars rising to different heights
scenes.animation: Ink block rises from 0 height on 'US'; '14 g' pops on '14'; teal block rises on 'compared'; '8 g' pops on '8'

scenes.line: Guidelines differ, so ask your doctor what's right for you.
scenes.visual: The two blocks tilt slightly apart; an ink speech bubble below reads 'Ask your doctor'
scenes.animation: Blocks rotate a few degrees apart on 'differ'; speech bubble pops with back.out on 'doctor'

scenes.line: One easy step: check the strength on the label before you pour.
scenes.visual: Flat bottle with a front label showing an 'ABV %' panel; a magnifier sweeps over it and a teal tick appears
scenes.animation: Bottle slides up at start; magnifier sweeps across on 'strength'; label panel highlights on 'label'; tick pops on 'pour'

scenes.line: Save this, and talk to your doctor if you're worried about how much you drink.
scenes.visual: Teal block with a bookmark icon; ink chip 'Talk to your doctor' below
scenes.animation: Bookmark drops and bounces on 'Save'; chip pops on 'doctor'

scenes.onScreenText: Not medical advice. Sources: NHS, CDC
